title: EIP-1559: London
scope: Local-only story, source verification and actual-art clue preparation. No remote writes and no artwork edits.

sources.title: EIP-1559 specification
sources.notes: Directly read. Establishes fee adjustment, burn, miner priority fees, and the conditional relationship between burn and issuance. CC0 notice present.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation: London Mainnet Announcement
verified_sections: As a miner, what do I need to do?
sources.notes: Directly read. Specifies activation block, included EIP and Devcon-city naming. Its expected date range is not used alone to establish the actual activation day.

sources.title: Ethereum upgrade history: London
sources.notes: Directly read. Records the actual 5 August 2021 activation and block 12,965,000.

sources.title: Ethereum.org: The Merge
sources.notes: Directly read. Confirms Mainnet used proof-of-work until the 15 September 2022 transition; the story only specifies September 2022.

sources.title: Ethereum.org: Gas and fees
verified_sections: Why can gas fees get so high?
sources.notes: Directly read for the continuing fee mechanism and demand-driven cost caveat. Present-day validator wording was not carried back into the 2021 story.

claims.text: London activated on 5 August 2021 at block 12,965,000 and included EIP-1559.
The base fee follows prior-block gas use relative to the target and is burned; priority fees went to miners.
London predates Mainnet's proof-of-stake transition in September 2022.
More predictable estimation does not ensure cheap transactions during high demand.
Burning does not guarantee an absolute fall in ETH supply; issuance also matters.
London's upgrade name references the city that hosted Devcon 1.
The dragon, traveller, bowls and physical coins are symbolic; Big Ben points to the name, not a physical activation site.
THE BASE FEE BURNS. is approved editorial card copy, not presented as a historical quotation.
